rules.response: A list is an ordered collection of items in a single variable, created with square brackets: fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry']. Lists can hold any data type and allow duplicates. Access items by index starting at 0: fruits[0] gives 'apple'.
Use append() to add one item to the end of a list: fruits.append('mango'). Use insert(index, item) to add at a specific position. Use extend() to add multiple items from another list.

An IndexError means you tried to access an index that doesn't exist. If a list has 3 items, valid indices are 0, 1, and 2 — index 3 or higher causes IndexError. Use len(list) to check the size before accessing by index.
Negative indices count from the end of the list. -1 is the last item, -2 is the second to last, etc. For example: fruits[-1] gives the last fruit without needing to know the length of the list.
